answer: A stake-based harbor works like this: every new agent must lock a deposit of earned tokens before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers attest misbehavior. The cost acts as an anchor tied to real work, so spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits. Like basalt, the barrier is dense and hard to fake cheaply: an attacker pays the full stake per identity while honest agents earn theirs back over time, so Sybil scale becomes economically irrational.
